title: Enhancing Matching of Training to Skills Needed by Industries and to Placement Outcomes
what_it_is: Enhancing Matching of Training to Skills Needed by Industries and to Placement Outcomes

sections.label: Skills-based hiring practices
sections.summary: Employers can build confidence for industry-relevant training by adopting skills-based hiring, supported by Career Health SG and a cybersecurity skills pathway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Employers can certainly create greater confidence for individuals to pursue industry-relevant training by adopting skills-based hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: These practices include identifying their skills needs, articulating them clearly in the job requirements and also recognising individuals' skills and competencies attained rather than relying only on credentials and qualifications alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: To further encourage employers to adopt skills-based hiring, the Ministry of Manpower, WSG and SSG have launched the Career Health SG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This initiative equips employers with tools and resources, including those developed by the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) to practise skills-first hiring and develop their workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: For example, the Singapore Computer Society, one of SSG's Skills Development Partners, launched the Skills Pathway for Cybersecurity last year, presenting a clearer career roadmap for individuals to enter the cybersecurity field or for existing cybersecurity professionals to upskill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: It brings together key employers in the sector to recognise the professional skills that individuals need to obtain to be considered for interviews and internships, and this can improve their employability too.

sections.label: Engaging tripartite partners on skills-based hiring
sections.summary: The government has no preferred sectors and will work with tripartite partners and IHRP to engage employers on skills-based hiring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I think this is in the context of Ms Jean See's question – reaching out to them so that they know the resources that are available that they can tap on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We do not have specific preferred sectors to develop this, but certainly we are very happy to work with our tripartite partners, including the Singapore National Employers' Federation, the National Trades Union Congress, the trade associations and chambers, and the Singapore Business Federation to help engage employers and companies out there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Another important partner would be IHRP, the HR professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We think that by strengthening their competency in applying skills-based hiring and employment practices, we can take the step further in promoting skills-based hiring in Singapore.
